sentences.zh: 泰始二年八月，詔曰：「此上旬，先帝棄天下日也，便以周年。

translations.literal: In the eighth month of the second year of Taishi, an edict said, "This first third of the month is the day on which the late emperor abandoned all under Heaven, and it is now the full year.
translations.idiomatic: In the eighth month of the second year of Taishi, an edict said, "This first third of the month is the day on which the late emperor abandoned all under Heaven, and it is now the full year.

sentences.zh: 吾煢煢，當復何時一得敘人子之情邪！

translations.literal: I am alone and bereft. At what time could I ever once express the feelings of a son!
translations.idiomatic: I am alone and bereft. At what time could I ever once express the feelings of a son!

sentences.zh: 思慕煩毒，欲詔陵瞻侍，以盡哀憤。

translations.literal: My longing and grief trouble and poison me, and I wish to order a visit and attendance at the mausoleum, in order to exhaust my grief and resentment.
translations.idiomatic: My longing and grief trouble and poison me, and I wish to order a visit and attendance at the mausoleum, in order to exhaust my grief and resentment.

sentences.zh: 主者具行備。」

translations.literal: Let the responsible officials fully prepare the procession."
translations.idiomatic: Let the responsible officials fully prepare the procession."

sentences.zh: 太宰安平王孚、尚書令裴秀、尚書僕射武陔等奏：「陛下至孝蒸蒸，哀思罔極。

translations.literal: Grand Steward Prince Fu of Anping, Director of the Secretariat Pei Xiu, Vice Director of the Secretariat Wu Gai, and others memorialized, "Your Majesty's utmost filial piety rises abundantly, and your grieving thoughts have no limit.
translations.idiomatic: Grand Steward Prince Fu of Anping, Director of the Secretariat Pei Xiu, Vice Director of the Secretariat Wu Gai, and others memorialized, "Your Majesty's utmost filial piety rises abundantly, and your grieving thoughts have no limit.

sentences.zh: 衰麻雖除，哀毀疏食，有損神和。

translations.literal: Although sackcloth and hemp have been removed, grieving self-injury and coarse food damage the harmony of the spirit.
translations.idiomatic: Although sackcloth and hemp have been removed, grieving self-injury and coarse food damage the harmony of the spirit.

sentences.zh: 今雖秋節，尚有餘暑，謁見山陵，悲感摧傷，群下竊用竦息，以為宜降抑聖情，以慰萬國。」

translations.literal: Now, although it is the autumn season, there is still remaining heat. To visit and see the mountain mausoleum would bring grief and feeling that crush and wound you. We below privately tremble and hold our breath, and consider it fitting that you lower and restrain the sacred feelings, in order to comfort the myriad states."
translations.idiomatic: Now, although it is the autumn season, there is still remaining heat. To visit and see the mountain mausoleum would bring grief and feeling that crush and wound you. We below privately tremble and hold our breath, and consider it fitting that you lower and restrain the sacred feelings, in order to comfort the myriad states."

sentences.zh: 詔曰：「孤煢忽爾，日月已周，痛慕摧感，永無逮及。

translations.literal: An edict said, "I was suddenly made orphaned and bereft, and the days and months have already completed the cycle. Pain and longing crush and move me; there is forever no way to reach him.
translations.idiomatic: An edict said, "I was suddenly made orphaned and bereft, and the days and months have already completed the cycle. Pain and longing crush and move me; there is forever no way to reach him.

sentences.zh: 欲瞻奉山陵，以敘哀憤，體氣自佳耳。

translations.literal: I wish to look upon and attend the mountain mausoleum, in order to express my grief and resentment. My physical energy is naturally still good.
translations.idiomatic: I wish to look upon and attend the mountain mausoleum, in order to express my grief and resentment. My physical energy is naturally still good.

sentences.zh: 又已涼，便當行，不得如所奏也。

translations.literal: Moreover, it is already cool, and I shall go at once. I cannot do as you memorialized.
translations.idiomatic: Moreover, it is already cool, and I shall go at once. I cannot do as you memorialized.

sentences.zh: 主者便具行備。」

translations.literal: Let the responsible officials fully prepare the procession at once."
translations.idiomatic: Let the responsible officials fully prepare the procession at once."

sentences.zh: 又詔曰：「漢文不使天下盡哀，亦帝王至謙之志。

translations.literal: Another edict said, "That Emperor Wen of Han did not make all under Heaven exhaust grief was also the supremely modest intent of an emperor and king.
translations.idiomatic: Another edict said, "That Emperor Wen of Han did not make all under Heaven exhaust grief was also the supremely modest intent of an emperor and king.

sentences.zh: 當見山陵，何心而無服，其以衰絰行。」

translations.literal: When I am to see the mountain mausoleum, with what heart could I be without mourning dress? Let me go wearing sackcloth and headband."
translations.idiomatic: When I am to see the mountain mausoleum, with what heart could I be without mourning dress? Let me go wearing sackcloth and headband."

sentences.zh: 孚等重奏曰：「臣聞上古喪期無數，後世乃有年月之漸。

translations.literal: Fu and the others again memorialized, "We your servants have heard that in high antiquity mourning terms had no fixed number, and only in later ages did there gradually come to be years and months.
translations.idiomatic: Fu and the others again memorialized, "We your servants have heard that in high antiquity mourning terms had no fixed number, and only in later ages did there gradually come to be years and months.

sentences.zh: 漢文帝隨時之義，制為短喪，傳之於後。

translations.literal: Emperor Wen of Han followed the meaning of the time, made a system of shortened mourning, and transmitted it to later ages.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Wen of Han followed the meaning of the time, made a system of shortened mourning, and transmitted it to later ages.

sentences.zh: 陛下以社稷宗廟之重，萬方億兆之故，既從權制，釋除衰麻，群臣百姓吉服，今者謁陵，以敘哀慕，若加衰絰，進退無當。

translations.literal: Because of the weight of the altars of soil and grain and the ancestral temple, and because of the countless people in the myriad regions, Your Majesty has already followed the expedient system, released and removed sackcloth and hemp, and the assembled ministers and hundred surnames wear auspicious dress. Now, in visiting the mausoleum to express grief and longing, if you add sackcloth and headband, neither advance nor retreat would be fitting.
translations.idiomatic: Because of the weight of the altars of soil and grain and the ancestral temple, and because of the countless people in the myriad regions, Your Majesty has already followed the expedient system, released and removed sackcloth and hemp, and the assembled ministers and hundred surnames wear auspicious dress. Now, in visiting the mausoleum to express grief and longing, if you add sackcloth and headband, neither advance nor retreat would be fitting.

sentences.zh: 不敢奉詔。」

translations.literal: We dare not receive and carry out the edict."
translations.idiomatic: We dare not receive and carry out the edict."

sentences.zh: 詔曰：「亦知不在此麻布耳。

translations.literal: An edict said, "I also know that it does not lie in this hempen cloth.
translations.idiomatic: An edict said, "I also know that it does not lie in this hempen cloth.

sentences.zh: 然人子情思，為欲令哀喪之物在身，蓋近情也。

translations.literal: Yet the feelings and thoughts of a son are such that he wants the things of grief and mourning to be on his body; this is probably close to the feeling.
translations.idiomatic: Yet the feelings and thoughts of a son are such that he wants the things of grief and mourning to be on his body; this is probably close to the feeling.

sentences.zh: 群臣自當案舊制。」

translations.literal: The assembled ministers should themselves follow the old system."
translations.idiomatic: The assembled ministers should themselves follow the old system."

sentences.zh: 孚等又奏曰：「臣聞聖人制作，必從時宜。

translations.literal: Fu and the others again memorialized, "We your servants have heard that when the sages made institutions, they always followed what was fitting to the time.
translations.idiomatic: Fu and the others again memorialized, "We your servants have heard that when the sages made institutions, they always followed what was fitting to the time.

sentences.zh: 故五帝殊樂，三王異禮，此古今所以不同，質文所以迭用也。

translations.literal: Therefore the Five Emperors differed in music, and the Three Kings differed in ritual. This is why ancient and modern are not the same, and why substance and refinement are used in alternation.
translations.idiomatic: Therefore the Five Emperors differed in music, and the Three Kings differed in ritual. This is why ancient and modern are not the same, and why substance and refinement are used in alternation.

sentences.zh: 陛下隨時之宜，既降心克己，俯就權制，既除衰麻，而行心喪之禮，今復制服，義無所依。

translations.literal: Your Majesty followed what was fitting to the time, lowered your heart and overcame yourself, bowed down to the expedient system, already removed sackcloth and hemp, and practiced the ritual of mourning in the heart. Now to again put on the regulated dress has no meaning on which to rely.
translations.idiomatic: Your Majesty followed what was fitting to the time, lowered your heart and overcame yourself, bowed down to the expedient system, already removed sackcloth and hemp, and practiced the ritual of mourning in the heart. Now to again put on the regulated dress has no meaning on which to rely.

sentences.zh: 若君服而臣不服，亦未之敢安也。

translations.literal: If the ruler wears mourning dress and the ministers do not, this too is not something we would dare consider at ease.
translations.idiomatic: If the ruler wears mourning dress and the ministers do not, this too is not something we would dare consider at ease.

sentences.zh: 參議宜如前奏。」

translations.literal: Our joint deliberation holds that it should be as in the previous memorial."
translations.idiomatic: Our joint deliberation holds that it should be as in the previous memorial."

sentences.zh: 詔曰：「患情不能跂及耳，衣服何在。

translations.literal: An edict said, "What I suffer from is only that my feelings cannot stretch to reach him; what does it have to do with clothing?
translations.idiomatic: An edict said, "What I suffer from is only that my feelings cannot stretch to reach him; what does it have to do with clothing?

sentences.zh: 諸君勤勤之至，豈苟相違。」，

translations.literal: You gentlemen are diligent to the utmost. How could I merely oppose you?"
translations.idiomatic: You gentlemen are diligent to the utmost. How could I merely oppose you?"

sentences.zh: 泰始四年，皇太后崩。

translations.literal: In the fourth year of Taishi, the Empress Dowager died.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth year of Taishi, the Empress Dowager died.

sentences.zh: 有司奏：「前代故事，倚廬中施白縑帳、蓐、素床，以布巾裹塊草，軺輦、版輿、細犢車皆施縑裏。」

translations.literal: The responsible offices memorialized, "Former-generation precedents set white silk curtains, mats, and a plain bed in the leaning hut, wrapped clods and grass in a cloth kerchief, and applied silk linings to the light carriage, plank carriage, and small-calf cart."
translations.idiomatic: The responsible offices memorialized, "Former-generation precedents set white silk curtains, mats, and a plain bed in the leaning hut, wrapped clods and grass in a cloth kerchief, and applied silk linings to the light carriage, plank carriage, and small-calf cart."

sentences.zh: 詔不聽，但令以布衣車而已，其餘居喪之制，不改禮文。

translations.literal: The edict did not consent; it ordered only plain-cloth carts; as for the rest of the dwelling-in-mourning system, it did not alter the ritual text.
translations.idiomatic: He refused the silks but allowed plain carts only, leaving every other mourning rule as written in the canon.

sentences.zh: 有司又奏：「大行皇太后當以四月二十五日安厝。

translations.literal: The responsible offices again memorialized, "The deceased Empress Dowager should be interred on the twenty-fifth day of the fourth month.
translations.idiomatic: The responsible offices again memorialized, "The deceased Empress Dowager should be interred on the twenty-fifth day of the fourth month.

sentences.zh: 故事，虞著衰服，既虞而除。

translations.literal: According to precedent, at the yu sacrifice one wears mourning dress, and after the yu sacrifice one removes it.
translations.idiomatic: According to precedent, at the yu sacrifice one wears mourning dress, and after the yu sacrifice one removes it.

sentences.zh: 其內外官僚皆就朝晡臨位，御除服訖，各還所次除衰服。」

translations.literal: Let the officials inside and outside all go to their mourning positions at morning and afternoon, and when the imperial removal of dress is complete, each return to his quarters and remove mourning dress."
translations.idiomatic: Let the officials inside and outside all go to their mourning positions at morning and afternoon, and when the imperial removal of dress is complete, each return to his quarters and remove mourning dress."

sentences.zh: 詔曰：「夫三年之喪，天下之達禮也。

translations.literal: An edict said, "The three-year mourning is the universally observed ritual throughout all under Heaven.
translations.idiomatic: An edict said, "The three-year mourning is the universally observed ritual throughout all under Heaven.

sentences.zh: 受終身之愛，而無數年之報，柰何葬而便即吉，情所不忍也。」

translations.literal: Having received a lifetime of love, yet making no repayment of several years: how could one be buried and then immediately return to felicity? My feeling cannot bear it."
translations.idiomatic: Having received a lifetime of love, yet making no repayment of several years: how could one be buried and then immediately return to felicity? My feeling cannot bear it."

sentences.zh: 有司又奏：「世有險易，道有洿隆，所遇之時異，誠有由然，非忽禮也。

translations.literal: The responsible offices again memorialized, "Ages have danger and ease, and the Way has hollows and heights. That the times encountered differ truly has reasons; it is not disregard for ritual.
translations.idiomatic: The responsible offices again memorialized, "Ages have danger and ease, and the Way has hollows and heights. That the times encountered differ truly has reasons; it is not disregard for ritual.

sentences.zh: 方今戎馬未散，王事至殷，更須聽斷，以熙庶績。

translations.literal: At present, war horses have not yet dispersed, and royal affairs are extremely urgent. It is further necessary to hear and decide matters, in order to brighten the many tasks.
translations.idiomatic: At present, war horses have not yet dispersed, and royal affairs are extremely urgent. It is further necessary to hear and decide matters, in order to brighten the many tasks.

sentences.zh: 昔周康王始登翌室，猶戴冕臨朝。

translations.literal: Formerly, when King Kang of Zhou first ascended the next chamber, he still wore the cap and robe and attended court.
translations.idiomatic: Formerly, when King Kang of Zhou first ascended the next chamber, he still wore the cap and robe and attended court.

sentences.zh: 降于漢魏，既葬除釋，諒闇之禮，自遠代而廢矣。

translations.literal: Down to Han and Wei, after burial mourning was removed and released, and the ritual of liang'an had been abandoned since distant ages.
translations.idiomatic: Down to Han and Wei, after burial mourning was removed and released, and the ritual of liang'an had been abandoned since distant ages.

sentences.zh: 惟陛下割高宗之制，從當時之宜。」

translations.literal: We only ask Your Majesty to cut back the system of Gaozong and follow what is fitting to the present time."
translations.idiomatic: We only ask Your Majesty to cut back the system of Gaozong and follow what is fitting to the present time."

sentences.zh: 詔曰：「夫三年之喪，所以盡情致禮，葬已便除，所不堪也。

translations.literal: An edict said, "The three-year mourning is how one exhausts feeling and brings ritual to completion. To remove it once burial is finished is what I cannot bear.
translations.idiomatic: An edict said, "The three-year mourning is how one exhausts feeling and brings ritual to completion. To remove it once burial is finished is what I cannot bear.

sentences.zh: 當敘吾哀懷，言用斷絕，柰何！

translations.literal: When I try to express my grief, words are cut off. What can I do!
translations.idiomatic: When I try to express my grief, words are cut off. What can I do!

sentences.zh: 柰何！」

translations.literal: What can I do!"
translations.idiomatic: What can I do!"

sentences.zh: 有司又固請。

translations.literal: The offices again firmly requested.
translations.idiomatic: The bureaus petitioned again, harder.

sentences.zh: 詔曰：「不能篤孝，勿以毀傷為憂也。

translations.literal: An edict said, "If I cannot be deeply filial, do not take self-injury as a worry.
translations.idiomatic: An edict said, "If I cannot be deeply filial, do not take self-injury as a worry.

sentences.zh: 誠知衣服末事耳，然今思存草土，率當以吉物奪之，乃所以重傷至心，非見念也。

translations.literal: I truly know that clothing is a minor matter. Yet now, when my thoughts are to remain with grass and earth, to take it away by means of auspicious things is precisely to wound the utmost heart again; it is not thinking of me.
translations.idiomatic: I truly know that clothing is a minor matter. Yet now, when my thoughts are to remain with grass and earth, to take it away by means of auspicious things is precisely to wound the utmost heart again; it is not thinking of me.

sentences.zh: 每代禮典質文皆不同耳，何為限以近制，使達喪闕然乎！」

translations.literal: In each age, ritual codes differ in substance and refinement. Why restrict me by a recent system and make the universal mourning deficient!"
translations.idiomatic: In each age, ritual codes differ in substance and refinement. Why restrict me by a recent system and make the universal mourning deficient!"

sentences.zh: 群臣又固請，帝流涕久之乃許。

translations.literal: The many ministers again firmly requested; the emperor wept a long time and then consented.
translations.idiomatic: Ministers pressed until he wept long and yielded.

sentences.zh: 文明皇后崩及武元楊后崩，天下將吏發哀三日止。

translations.literal: When Empress Dowager Wenming died and when Empress Wu-Yuan Yang died, officers throughout the realm raised mourning for three days and then stopped.
translations.idiomatic: When Empress Dowager Yuan died and when Empress Yang the consort of Wu died, officers empire-wide wailed three days only.

sentences.zh: 穆帝崩，哀帝立。

translations.literal: When Emperor Mu died, Emperor Ai was enthroned.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Ai succeeded when Emperor Mu passed.

sentences.zh: 帝于穆帝為從父昆弟，穆帝舅褚歆有表，中書答表朝廷無其儀，詔下議。

translations.literal: The emperor toward Emperor Mu was a father's-brother's son; Emperor Mu's maternal uncle Chu Xin submitted a memorial; the Secretariat replied to the memorial that the court had no such precedent, and an edict sent the matter down for deliberation.
translations.idiomatic: Ai was Mu's cousin; Mu's uncle Chu Xin asked how to mourn; the Secretariat said no rule existed and the throne sent the case to debate.

sentences.zh: 尚書僕射江虨等四人並云，閔僖兄弟也，而為父子，則哀帝應為帝嗣。

translations.literal: Vice Minister of the Masters of Writing Jiang Pin and four others together said: 'Duke Min and Duke Xi were brothers yet treated as father and son—therefore Emperor Ai ought to follow the emperor's line of succession.'
translations.idiomatic: Jiang Pin and four others cited Duke Min and Duke Xi of Lu—brothers treated as father and son—and argued Ai should continue Cheng's line.

sentences.zh: 衛軍王述等二十五人云「成帝不私親愛，越授天倫，康帝受命顯宗。

translations.literal: Guard General Wang Shu and twenty-five others said, "Emperor Cheng did not privately favor his own loved ones, but passed beyond natural kinship in conferring the succession, and Emperor Kang received the command from Xianzong.
translations.idiomatic: Guard General Wang Shu and twenty-five others said, "Emperor Cheng did not privately favor his own loved ones, but passed beyond natural kinship in conferring the succession, and Emperor Kang received the command from Xianzong.

sentences.zh: 社稷之重，已移所授，纂承之序，宜繼康皇。」

translations.literal: The weight of the altars of soil and grain had already moved to the one who received it, and in the sequence of succession it is fitting to continue Emperor Kang."
translations.idiomatic: The weight of the altars of soil and grain had already moved to the one who received it, and in the sequence of succession it is fitting to continue Emperor Kang."

sentences.zh: 尚書謝奉等六人云：「繼體之正，宜本天屬，考之人情，宜繼顯宗也。」

translations.literal: Xie Feng of the Secretariat and six others said, "The correctness of inheriting the body should be rooted in Heaven-given kinship. Examining it according to human feeling, it is fitting to continue Xianzong."
translations.idiomatic: Xie Feng of the Secretariat and six others said, "The correctness of inheriting the body should be rooted in Heaven-given kinship. Examining it according to human feeling, it is fitting to continue Xianzong."

sentences.zh: 詔從述等議，上繼顯宗。

translations.literal: The edict followed Wang Shu and the others' debate and ordered succession to continue Emperor Yuan.
translations.idiomatic: The edict sided with Wang Shu and made Ai heir to Emperor Yuan.

sentences.zh: 寧康二年七月，簡文帝崩再周而遇閏。

translations.literal: In the second year of Ningkang, in the seventh month Emperor Jianwen died—the second full mourning cycle met an intercalary month.
translations.idiomatic: In the second year of Ningkang, in the seventh month, Emperor Jianwen died just as the second mourning round collided with an intercalary month.

sentences.zh: 博士謝攸、孔粲議：「魯襄二十八年十二月乙未，楚子卒，實閏月而言十二月者，附正於前月也。

translations.literal: Erudites Xie You and Kong Can deliberated, "In the twenty-eighth year of Duke Xiang of Lu, in the twelfth month, yiwei, the viscount of Chu died. It was actually an intercalary month, but saying twelfth month attached the regular designation to the preceding month.
translations.idiomatic: Erudites Xie You and Kong Can deliberated, "In the twenty-eighth year of Duke Xiang of Lu, in the twelfth month, yiwei, the viscount of Chu died. It was actually an intercalary month, but saying twelfth month attached the regular designation to the preceding month.

sentences.zh: 喪事先遠，則應用博士吳商之言，以閏月祥。」

translations.literal: For mourning affairs, one first chooses what is distant; therefore one should use the words of Erudite Wu Shang and hold the xiang sacrifice in the intercalary month."
translations.idiomatic: For mourning affairs, one first chooses what is distant; therefore one should use the words of Erudite Wu Shang and hold the xiang sacrifice in the intercalary month."

sentences.zh: 尚書僕射謝安、中領軍王劭、散騎常侍鄭襲、右衛將軍殷康、驍騎將軍袁宏、散騎侍郎殷茂、中書郎車胤、左丞劉遵、吏部郎劉耽意皆同。

translations.literal: Vice Minister of the Masters of Writing Xie An, Central Army commander Wang Shao, Cavalier Attendant-in-ordinary Zheng Xi, General of the Right Guard Yin Kang, General of Swift Cavalry Yuan Hong, Cavalier Gentleman Yin Mao, Palace Secretariat Secretary Che Yin, Left Assistant Liu Zun, Personnel Section chief Liu Dan—all agreed.
translations.idiomatic: Xie An, Wang Shao, Zheng Xi, Yin Kang, Yuan Hong, Yin Mao, Che Yin, Liu Zun, and Liu Dan concurred.

sentences.zh: 康曰：「過七月而未及八月，豈可謂之逾期。

translations.literal: Yin Kang said, "To pass the seventh month but not yet reach the eighth: how could this be called exceeding the term?
translations.idiomatic: Yin Kang said, "To pass the seventh month but not yet reach the eighth: how could this be called exceeding the term?

sentences.zh: 必所不了，則當從其重者。」

translations.literal: If it truly cannot be settled, then one should follow the weightier option."
translations.idiomatic: If it truly cannot be settled, then one should follow the weightier option."

sentences.zh: 宏曰：「假值閏十二月而不取者，此則歲未終，固不可得矣。

translations.literal: Yuan Hong said, "If it happened to be an intercalary twelfth month and one did not take it, then the year would not yet be complete, and this certainly could not be done.
translations.idiomatic: Yuan Hong said, "If it happened to be an intercalary twelfth month and one did not take it, then the year would not yet be complete, and this certainly could not be done.

sentences.zh: 《漢書》以閏為後九月，明其同體也。」

translations.literal: The Han shu treats an intercalary month as a later ninth month, showing that it is of the same body."
translations.idiomatic: The Han shu treats an intercalary month as a later ninth month, showing that it is of the same body."

sentences.zh: 襲曰：「中宗、肅祖皆以閏月崩，祥除之變皆用閏之後月。

translations.literal: Zheng Xi said, "Zhongzong and Suzong both died in intercalary months, and in the changes of xiang sacrifice and removal, all used the month after the intercalary month.
translations.idiomatic: Zheng Xi said, "Zhongzong and Suzong both died in intercalary months, and in the changes of xiang sacrifice and removal, all used the month after the intercalary month.

sentences.zh: 先朝尚用閏之後月，今閏附七月，取之何疑，亦合遠日申情之言。

translations.literal: The former court still used the month after the intercalary month. Now the intercalary month is attached to the seventh month; what doubt is there in taking it? This also accords with the statement that a distant day extends the feeling.
translations.idiomatic: The former court still used the month after the intercalary month. Now the intercalary month is attached to the seventh month; what doubt is there in taking it? This also accords with the statement that a distant day extends the feeling.

sentences.zh: 又閏是後七而非八也，豈逾月之嫌乎！」

translations.literal: Moreover, the intercalary month is after the seventh and is not the eighth; how could there be suspicion of exceeding the month!"
translations.idiomatic: Moreover, the intercalary month is after the seventh and is not the eighth; how could there be suspicion of exceeding the month!"

sentences.zh: 尚書令王彪之、侍中王混、中丞譙王恬、右丞戴謐等議異，彪之曰：「吳商中才小官，非名賢碩儒、公輔重臣、為時所準則者。

translations.literal: Director of the Secretariat Wang Biaozhi, Palace Attendant Wang Hun, Censor-in-Chief Prince Tian of Qiao, Right Assistant Director Dai Mi, and others deliberated differently. Biaozhi said, "Wu Shang was a man of middling talent and a minor official, not a famous worthy, great classicist, high minister, or weighty servant whom the age should take as a standard.
translations.idiomatic: Director of the Secretariat Wang Biaozhi, Palace Attendant Wang Hun, Censor-in-Chief Prince Tian of Qiao, Right Assistant Director Dai Mi, and others deliberated differently. Biaozhi said, "Wu Shang was a man of middling talent and a minor official, not a famous worthy, great classicist, high minister, or weighty servant whom the age should take as a standard.

sentences.zh: 又取閏無證據，直攬遠日之義，越祥忌，限外取，不合卜遠之理。

translations.literal: Moreover, taking the intercalary month has no evidence. It merely seizes on the meaning of the distant day, passes beyond the xiang taboo, and takes something outside the limit; this does not accord with the principle of divining the distant day.
translations.idiomatic: Moreover, taking the intercalary month has no evidence. It merely seizes on the meaning of the distant day, passes beyond the xiang taboo, and takes something outside the limit; this does not accord with the principle of divining the distant day.

sentences.zh: 又丞相桓公嘗論云，《禮》二十五月大祥。

translations.literal: Furthermore, Chancellor Huan once argued that according to ritual the great xiang sacrifice is in the twenty-fifth month.
translations.idiomatic: Furthermore, Chancellor Huan once argued that according to ritual the great xiang sacrifice is in the twenty-fifth month.

sentences.zh: 何緣越期取閏，乃二十六月乎？」

translations.literal: On what basis would one pass beyond the term and take the intercalary month, making it the twenty-sixth month?"
translations.idiomatic: On what basis would one pass beyond the term and take the intercalary month, making it the twenty-sixth month?"

sentences.zh: 於是啟曰：「或以閏附七月，宜用閏月除者。

translations.literal: Thereupon they submitted, "Some consider that because the intercalary month is attached to the seventh month, the intercalary month should be used for removal.
translations.idiomatic: Thereupon they submitted, "Some consider that because the intercalary month is attached to the seventh month, the intercalary month should be used for removal.

sentences.zh: 或以閏名雖除七月，而實以三旬別為一月，故應以七月除者。

translations.literal: Others consider that although the intercalary month is named as attached to the seventh month, in reality the three ten-day periods separately make one month, and therefore the seventh month should be used for removal.
translations.idiomatic: Others consider that although the intercalary month is named as attached to the seventh month, in reality the three ten-day periods separately make one month, and therefore the seventh month should be used for removal.

sentences.zh: 臣等與中軍將軍沖參詳，一代大禮，宜準經典。

translations.literal: We your servants, together with General of the Central Army Chong, have examined the matter in detail. A great ritual of one age should take the classics as its standard.
translations.idiomatic: We your servants, together with General of the Central Army Chong, have examined the matter in detail. A great ritual of one age should take the classics as its standard.

sentences.zh: 三年之喪，十三月而練，二十五月而畢，《禮》之明文也。

translations.literal: For the three-year mourning, the lian sacrifice is in the thirteenth month, and it is completed in the twenty-fifth month; this is the clear text of the rites.
translations.idiomatic: For the three-year mourning, the lian sacrifice is in the thirteenth month, and it is completed in the twenty-fifth month; this is the clear text of the rites.

sentences.zh: 《陽秋》之義，閏在年內，則略而不數。

translations.literal: According to the meaning of the Yangqiu, when an intercalary month is inside the year, it is omitted and not counted.
translations.idiomatic: According to the meaning of the Yangqiu, when an intercalary month is inside the year, it is omitted and not counted.

sentences.zh: 明閏在年外，則不應取之以越期忌之重，禮制祥除必正期月故也。」

translations.literal: It is clear that when the intercalary month is outside the year, one should not take it and thereby exceed the weight of the term and taboo, because the ritual system for xiang sacrifice and removal must correct the numbered months."
translations.idiomatic: It is clear that when the intercalary month is outside the year, one should not take it and thereby exceed the weight of the term and taboo, because the ritual system for xiang sacrifice and removal must correct the numbered months."

sentences.zh: 己酉晦，帝除縞即吉。

translations.literal: On jiyou, the last day of the month, the emperor shed mourning white silk and returned to auspicious dress.'
translations.idiomatic: On jiyou, month-end, the sovereign left white mourning and resumed felicity garb.

sentences.zh: 徐廣論曰：「凡辨義詳理，無顯據明文可以折中奪易，則非疑如何。

translations.literal: Xu Guang's discussion said, "In general, when distinguishing meaning and detailing principle, if there is no manifest evidence or clear text by which to decide and overturn the matter, then how can it not be doubtful?
translations.idiomatic: Xu Guang's discussion said, "In general, when distinguishing meaning and detailing principle, if there is no manifest evidence or clear text by which to decide and overturn the matter, then how can it not be doubtful?

sentences.zh: 禮疑從重，喪易甯戚，順情通物，固有成言矣。

translations.literal: When ritual is doubtful, one follows the weightier option; in mourning, when changing, one prefers grief. To follow feeling and comprehend things certainly already has established sayings.
translations.idiomatic: When ritual is doubtful, one follows the weightier option; in mourning, when changing, one prefers grief. To follow feeling and comprehend things certainly already has established sayings.

sentences.zh: 彪之不能徵援正義，有以相屈，但以名位格人，君子虛受，心無適莫，豈其然哉！

translations.literal: Biaozhi could not cite and invoke correct meaning in a way that would make others yield, but only used name and rank to restrain people. The gentleman receives emptily, and in his heart has no fixed leaning; how could this be so!
translations.idiomatic: Biaozhi could not cite and invoke correct meaning in a way that would make others yield, but only used name and rank to restrain people. The gentleman receives emptily, and in his heart has no fixed leaning; how could this be so!

sentences.zh: 執政從而行之，其殆過矣。」

translations.literal: Those who held government followed and carried it out; this was probably an error."
translations.idiomatic: Those who held government followed and carried it out; this was probably an error."

sentences.zh: 魏武以正月崩，魏文以其年七月設妓樂百戲，是則魏不以喪廢樂也。

translations.literal: Wei Wu died in the first month; Wei Wen in that year's seventh month set singing-girls and the hundred entertainments—therefore Wei did not cancel music because of mourning.
translations.idiomatic: Cao Cao died in the first month; Cao Pi still staged troupes and acrobats that seventh month—so Wei never treated mourning as a reason to silence the bands.

sentences.zh: 武帝以來，國有大喪，輒廢樂終三年。

translations.literal: From Emperor Wu onward, whenever the state had great mourning, court music was suspended for the full three years.
translations.idiomatic: Under Emperor Sima Yan, every dynastic bereavement silenced the orchestras for three years.

sentences.zh: 惠帝太安元年，太子喪未除，及元會亦廢樂。

translations.literal: In the first year of Taian under Emperor Hui, the crown prince's mourning was not yet removed—yet for the New Year court assembly music was likewise suspended.
translations.idiomatic: In Emperor Hui's Taian era, while the heir still wore mourning, the Yuan-day levee went without music.

sentences.zh: 穆帝永和中，為中原山陵未修復，頻年元會廢樂。

translations.literal: During Yonghe under Emperor Mu, because the imperial tombs on the Central Plain were not yet repaired, for successive years the Yuan assembly suspended music.
translations.idiomatic: Yonghe years saw the New Year court go silent while Luoyang's tombs lay in ruins.

sentences.zh: 是時太后臨朝，后父褚裒薨，元會又廢樂也。

translations.literal: At that time the empress dowager presided at court; the empress's father Chu Pou died—the Yuan assembly again suspended music.
translations.idiomatic: The regent's father Chu Pou died that same span, so the levee stayed mute again.

sentences.zh: 孝武太元六年，為皇后王氏喪，亦廢樂。

translations.literal: In the sixth year of Taiyuan under Emperor Xiaowu, during mourning for Empress Wang, music was likewise suspended.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixth year of Taiyuan under Emperor Xiaowu, during mourning for Empress Wang, music was likewise suspended.

sentences.zh: 孝武崩，太傅錄尚書會稽王道子議：「山陵之後，通婚嫁不得作樂，以一期為斷。」

translations.literal: When Xiaowu died, Grand Tutor concurrently recording Masters of Writing the Prince of Guiji, Sima Daozi, debated: 'After the imperial tomb is closed, weddings may proceed but without music—take one full cycle as the limit.'"
translations.idiomatic: When Xiaowu died, Grand Tutor concurrently recording Masters of Writing the Prince of Guiji, Sima Daozi, debated: 'After the imperial tomb is closed, weddings may proceed but without music—take one full cycle as the limit.'"

sentences.zh: 漢儀，太皇太后、皇太后崩，長樂太僕、少府大長秋典喪事，三公奉制度，他皆如禮。

translations.literal: Han regulations: when the grand empress dowager or empress dowager died, the Director of Changle, the Grand Coachman, the Grand Provisioner, and the Greater Chief of Staff managed funeral affairs; the Three Dukes presented the statutory scheme; everything else followed ritual.
translations.idiomatic: Han statute put the inner-palace stewards in charge of a dowager's obsequies while the Three Dukes supplied the legal template.

sentences.zh: 魏晉亦同天子之儀，

translations.literal: Wei and Jin likewise matched the Son of Heaven's observances.
translations.idiomatic: Wei and Jin copied the same imperial funeral code.

sentences.zh: 于時外內卒聞預異議，多怪之。

translations.literal: At that time, inside and outside the court, upon hearing Yu's different opinion, most thought it strange.
translations.idiomatic: Court and camp alike thought Du Yu's view bizarre.

sentences.zh: 或者乃謂其違禮以合時。

translations.literal: Some even said he violated ritual to suit the times.
translations.idiomatic: Some accused him of bending the canon to please fashion.

sentences.zh: 時預亦不自解說，退使博士段暢博采典籍，為之證據，令大義著明，足以垂示將來。

translations.literal: At the time Yu also did not explain himself; he retired and ordered Erudite Duan Chang broadly to gather classics and canons as evidence for him, so that the great meaning would shine clearly and suffice to instruct posterity.
translations.idiomatic: Du Yu said little himself but told Duan Chang to mine the classics for proofs that would settle the debate for later ages.

sentences.zh: 暢承預旨，遂撰集書傳舊文，條諸實事成言，以為定證，以弘指趣。

translations.literal: Chang received Yu's intent, then compiled transmitted old texts, itemizing verified events into sayings, as fixed proofs, to broaden the purport.
translations.idiomatic: Duan Chang collated precedents and tagged each with a gloss to anchor Du Yu's thesis.

sentences.zh: 其傳記有與今議同者，亦具列之，博舉二隅，明其會歸，以證斯事。

translations.literal: Wherever records agreed with today's debate, he likewise listed them in full—broadly raising two angles, clarifying their convergence, to prove this affair.
translations.idiomatic: He cited parallels that matched the new rule and mapped how they converged on one conclusion.

sentences.zh: 文多不載。

translations.literal: The text is extensive and is not recorded here.
translations.idiomatic: The compilation ran long and is omitted here.

sentences.zh: 武帝楊悼皇后既母養懷帝，后遇難時，懷帝尚幼，及即位，中詔述后恩愛。

translations.literal: Empress Yang Dao of Emperor Wu had already mother-nurtured Emperor Huai; when she later met violent death, Emperor Huai was still young; when he ascended, an inner edict recounted the empress's kindness and love.
translations.idiomatic: Empress Yang had raised the future Emperor Huai; when she was killed he was still a child, and on enthronement he issued a palace rescript praising her care.

sentences.zh: 及后祖載，群官議帝應為追制服，或以庶母慈己，依禮制小功五月，或以謂慈母服如母服齊衰者，眾議不同。

translations.literal: When later her funeral train departed, the many offices debated whether the emperor ought wear retroactive mourning—or some said because a concubine-mother had loved him, by ritual he should wear xiao gong five months—or some said foster-mother mourning like a mother's qi-cui—the many opinions differed.
translations.idiomatic: At her cortège the ministries split: some wanted retroactive weeds, some cited a nurturing concubine's xiao gong, some equated her to a legal mother in qi-cui.

sentences.zh: 閭丘沖議云：「楊后母養聖上，蓋以曲情。

translations.literal: Luqiu Chong debated: 'Empress Yang mother-nurtured the sage ascendant—generally out of special affection.
translations.idiomatic: Luqiu Chong debated: 'Empress Yang mother-nurtured the sage ascendant—generally out of special affection.

sentences.zh: 今以恩禮追崇，不配世祖廟。

translations.literal: Now by kindness and ritual we posthumously honor her—not pairing her in Emperor Shizu's temple.
translations.idiomatic: Now by kindness and ritual we posthumously honor her—not pairing her in Emperor Shizu's temple.

sentences.zh: 王者無慈養之服，謂宜祖載之日，可三朝素服發哀而已。」

translations.literal: For kings there is no garment for 'foster nurturing'; I say on the day of the funeral train, three court sessions in plain dress to raise mourning is enough.'
translations.idiomatic: For kings there is no garment for 'foster nurturing'; I say on the day of the funeral train, three court sessions in plain dress to raise mourning is enough.'

sentences.zh: 於是從之。

translations.literal: Thereupon [the court] followed this.'"
translations.idiomatic: The throne accepted his view.

sentences.zh: 康帝建元元年正月晦，成恭杜皇后周忌，有司奏，至尊期年應改服。

translations.literal: On the last day of the first month in the first year of Jianyuan under Emperor Kang, the full-year anniversary of Empress Chenggong Du arrived, and the responsible offices memorialized that after the full year the sovereign should change garments.
translations.idiomatic: On the last day of the first month in the first year of Jianyuan under Emperor Kang, the full-year anniversary of Empress Chenggong Du arrived, and the responsible offices memorialized that after the full year the sovereign should change garments.

sentences.zh: 詔曰：「君親，名教之重也，權制出於近代耳。」

translations.literal: The edict said: 'Lord and parent are what name-teaching esteems most heavily—expedient regulation arose only in recent generations.'
translations.idiomatic: The edict said: 'Lord and parent are what name-teaching esteems most heavily—expedient regulation arose only in recent generations.'

sentences.zh: 於是素服如舊，固非漢魏之典也，

translations.literal: Thereupon plain dress as before—indeed this is not Han-Wei canonical precedent.'"
translations.idiomatic: He kept plain dress anyway—far from Han or Wei orthodoxy.

sentences.zh: 隆安四年，孝武太皇太后李氏崩，疑所服。

translations.literal: In the fourth year of Long'an, [The narrative continues:] Grand Empress Dowager Li of Xiaowu died—there was doubt about the garment.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth year of Long'an, when Grand Empress Dowager Li died, the court disputed the proper weeds.

sentences.zh: 尚書左僕射何澄、右僕射王雅、尚書車胤、孔安國、祠部郎徐廣議、太皇太后名位允正，體同皇極，理制備盡，情禮彌申。

translations.literal: Left Vice Minister He Cheng, right Vice Minister Wang Ya, ministers Che Yin, Kong Anguo, and Xu Guang of the Ritual Section debated: the grand empress dowager's title and rank are correct—her body matches the supreme pole—principle and system are complete, feeling and ritual further extend.
translations.idiomatic: He Cheng, Wang Ya, Che Yin, Kong Anguo, and Xu Guang argued her title was orthodox, her station matched the pole, and both law and sentiment demanded full mourning.

sentences.zh: 《陽秋》之義，母以子貴，既稱夫人，禮服從正。

translations.literal: The Spring and Autumn meaning: the mother is honored through the son—once she is titled lady, ritual garments follow correctness.
translations.idiomatic: The Zuo principle 'mother honored by son' means a titled consort takes the full garment schedule.

sentences.zh: 故成風顯夫人之號，文公服三年之喪。

translations.literal: Therefore Cheng Feng bore the lady's title; Duke Wen observed three years' mourning.
translations.idiomatic: Hence Duke Wen wore three years for Lady Chengfeng once she was titled mother.

sentences.zh: 子于父之所生，體尊義重。

translations.literal: The son toward the parent who bore him—body venerable, meaning heavy.
translations.idiomatic: A son owes the birth parent both dignity and deep obligation.

sentences.zh: 且禮，祖不厭孫，固宜遂服無屈，而緣情立制。

translations.literal: Moreover by ritual the founding ancestor does not suppress the grandson—therefore it is fitting to follow the garment without bending, yet by feeling establish regulation.
translations.idiomatic: Ancestors do not override grandsons, so nothing in the canon forces a reduction, though feeling may shape the grade.

sentences.zh: 若嫌明文不存，則疑斯從重，謂應同于為祖母后齊衰期。

translations.literal: If one suspects the clear text does not survive, then in doubt follow the heavier—I say one ought match wearing qi-cui one cycle for a grandmother-empress.
translations.idiomatic: Where scripture is unclear, choose the heavier rule—here that means qi-cui for a grandmother-empress.

sentences.zh: 永安皇后無服，但一舉哀，百官亦一期。」

translations.literal: Empress Yong'an had no garment—only once raised mourning; the hundred officials likewise one cycle.'
translations.idiomatic: Empress Yong'an had no garment—only once raised mourning; the hundred officials likewise one cycle.'

sentences.zh: 詔可。

translations.literal: The edict approved.'"
translations.idiomatic: The rescript said yes.

sentences.zh: 孝武帝太元十五年，淑媛陳氏卒，皇太子所生也。

translations.literal: In the fifteenth year of Taiyuan under Emperor Xiaowu, Honored Lady Chen died; she was the birth mother of the crown prince.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifteenth year of Taiyuan under Emperor Xiaowu, Honored Lady Chen died; she was the birth mother of the crown prince.

sentences.zh: 有司參詳母以子貴，贈淑媛為夫人，置家令典喪事。

translations.literal: The offices deliberated in detail: the mother is honored through the son—posthumously honored the Honored Lady as lady—established a household steward to manage funeral affairs.
translations.idiomatic: the ministries invoked 'mother honored by son,' raised her to Lady, and assigned a household steward for the funeral.

sentences.zh: 太子前衛率徐邈議：「《喪服傳》稱與尊者為體，則不服其私親。

translations.literal: Former crown-prince guard commander Xu Miao debated: "The Mourning Garments Commentary states that when one forms one body with the honored person, then one does not wear mourning for one's private kin.
translations.idiomatic: Former crown-prince guard commander Xu Miao debated: "The Mourning Garments Commentary states that when one forms one body with the honored person, then one does not wear mourning for one's private kin.

sentences.zh: 又，君父所不服，子亦不敢服。

translations.literal: Moreover, what lord and father does not wear, the son likewise dare not wear.
translations.idiomatic: Moreover, what lord and father does not wear, the son likewise dare not wear.

sentences.zh: 故王公妾子服其所生母練冠麻衣，既葬而除，非五服之常，則謂之無服。」

translations.literal: Therefore royal lords' sons by concubines wear for their birth mothers lien cap and hemp cloth—once buried then remove—not among the five garments' constant norms—then it is called having no garment."
translations.idiomatic: Therefore royal lords' sons by concubines wear for their birth mothers lien cap and hemp cloth—once buried then remove—not among the five garments' constant norms—then it is called having no garment."

sentences.zh: 從之，

translations.literal: This was followed.
translations.idiomatic: The court accepted his reading.

sentences.zh: 太元二十一年，孝武帝崩，孝武太后制三年之服。

translations.literal: In the twenty-first year of Taiyuan, Emperor Xiaowu died, and Empress Dowager Xiaowu established three-year mourning dress.
translations.idiomatic: In the twenty-first year of Taiyuan, Emperor Xiaowu died, and Empress Dowager Xiaowu established three-year mourning dress.

sentences.zh: 惠帝太安元年三月，皇太孫尚薨。

translations.literal: In the third month of the first year of Taian under Emperor Hui, the imperial grandson-heir Shang died.
translations.idiomatic: In the third month of the first year of Taian under Emperor Hui, the imperial grandson-heir Shang died.

sentences.zh: 有司奏，御服齊衰期。

translations.literal: The offices memorialized that the sovereign should wear qi-cui for one full year (qi).
translations.idiomatic: The authorities asked that the emperor observe qi-cui mourning for the standard one-year term.

sentences.zh: 詔下通議。

translations.literal: An edict ordered general court deliberation.
translations.idiomatic: The throne sent down an edict for the whole bureaucracy to debate the matter.

sentences.zh: 散騎常侍謝衡以為：「諸侯之太子，誓與未誓，尊卑體殊。

translations.literal: Cavalier attendant-in-ordinary Xie Heng held: "For a feudal lord's heir apparent, sworn presentation versus not yet sworn—the honored base and bodily tie differ.
translations.idiomatic: Cavalier attendant-in-ordinary Xie Heng held: "For a feudal lord's heir apparent, sworn presentation versus not yet sworn—the honored base and bodily tie differ.

sentences.zh: 《喪服》云為嫡子長殤，謂未誓也，已誓則不殤也。」

translations.literal: The Mourning Garments [canon] states mourning for the eldest legitimate son's long shang means not yet sworn; once sworn then it is not [counted as] shang."
translations.idiomatic: The Mourning Garments [canon] states mourning for the eldest legitimate son's long shang means not yet sworn; once sworn then it is not [counted as] shang."

sentences.zh: 中書令卞粹曰：「太子始生，故已尊重，不待命誓。

translations.literal: Minister of the Secretariat Bian Cui said: "The heir apparent from birth is therefore already honored high—does not await mandate-swearing.
translations.idiomatic: Minister of the Secretariat Bian Cui said: "The heir apparent from birth is therefore already honored high—does not await mandate-swearing.

sentences.zh: 若衡議已誓不殤，則無服之子當斬衰三年；

translations.literal: If by Xie's debate sworn means not shang, then the son for whom there is no [shang-scale] garment ought wear zhan-cui three years;
translations.idiomatic: If by Xie's debate sworn means not shang, then the son for whom there is no [shang-scale] garment ought wear zhan-cui three years;

sentences.zh: 未誓而殤，則雖十九當大功九月。

translations.literal: not sworn and [dies as] shang, then though age nineteen ought wear da gong nine months.
translations.idiomatic: not sworn and [dies as] shang, then though age nineteen ought wear da gong nine months.

sentences.zh: 誓與未誓，其為升降也微；

translations.literal: Sworn and not sworn—the rise and fall therein is slight;
translations.idiomatic: Sworn and not sworn—the rise and fall therein is slight;

sentences.zh: 斬衰與大功，其為輕重也遠。

translations.literal: zhan-cui and da gong—the light and heavy therein is far apart.
translations.idiomatic: zhan-cui and da gong—the light and heavy therein is far apart.

sentences.zh: 而今注云『諸侯不降嫡殤重』。

translations.literal: Yet now the commentary states 'feudal lords do not lower the weight of legitimate-son shang.'
translations.idiomatic: Yet now the commentary states 'feudal lords do not lower the weight of legitimate-son shang.'

sentences.zh: 嫌于無服，以大功為重嫡之服，則雖誓，無復有三年之理明矣。

translations.literal: Loath to [say] no garment, taking da gong as the garment weighting the legitimate heir—then though sworn, there is no longer principle for three years—this is clear.
translations.idiomatic: Loath to [say] no garment, taking da gong as the garment weighting the legitimate heir—then though sworn, there is no longer principle for three years—this is clear.

sentences.zh: 男能衛社稷，女能奉婦道，以可成之年而有已成之事，故可無殤，非孩齔之謂也。

translations.literal: When a male can guard altars of soil and grain and a female can uphold the wifely way—in years when completion is possible yet matters already accomplished—therefore may be without shang—it does not mean infant teeth.
translations.idiomatic: When a male can guard altars of soil and grain and a female can uphold the wifely way—in years when completion is possible yet matters already accomplished—therefore may be without shang—it does not mean infant teeth.

sentences.zh: 為殤後者尊之如父，猶無所加而止殤服，況以天子之尊，而為無服之殤行成人之制邪！

translations.literal: One who succeeds a shang [decedent] honors him like a father—still adds nothing and stops at shang garment—how much more with Heaven's Son's honor to enact adult norms for a shang without garment!
translations.idiomatic: One who succeeds a shang [decedent] honors him like a father—still adds nothing and stops at shang garment—how much more with Heaven's Son's honor to enact adult norms for a shang without garment!

sentences.zh: 凡諸宜重之殤，皆士大夫不加服，而令至尊獨居其重，未之前聞也。」

translations.literal: All shangs that ought be weighted—great officers add no garment—yet to make the supremacy alone bear the weight—never before heard."
translations.idiomatic: All shangs that ought be weighted—great officers add no garment—yet to make the supremacy alone bear the weight—never before heard."

sentences.zh: 博士蔡克同粹。

translations.literal: Erudite Cai Ke agreed with Bian Cui.
translations.idiomatic: Court erudite Cai Ke sided with Bian Cui.

sentences.zh: 秘書監摯虞云：「太子初生，舉以成人之禮，則殤理除矣。

translations.literal: Director of the Palace Library Zhi Yu said: "The heir apparent from birth is raised with adult rites—then shang principle is removed.
translations.idiomatic: Director of the Palace Library Zhi Yu said: "The heir apparent from birth is raised with adult rites—then shang principle is removed.

sentences.zh: 太孫亦體君傳重，由位成而服，全非以年也。

translations.literal: The grand heir likewise forms one body with the lord and transmits weight—garments follow from position achieved, wholly not by age.
translations.idiomatic: The grand heir likewise forms one body with the lord and transmits weight—garments follow from position achieved, wholly not by age.

sentences.zh: 天子無服殤之義，絕期故也。」

translations.literal: The Son of Heaven has no principle of wearing [mourning for] shang—because [such ties] are cut off at one full cycle (qi)."
translations.idiomatic: The Son of Heaven has no principle of wearing [mourning for] shang—because [such ties] are cut off at one full cycle (qi)."

sentences.zh: 於是從之。

translations.literal: Thereupon [the court] followed this.
translations.idiomatic: The court adopted this view.

sentences.zh: 《喪服記》，公為所寓，齊衰三月。

translations.literal: The Mourning Garments Record states that a lord for a host to whom he lodges wears qi-cui three months.
translations.idiomatic: Classical text still gives three months of qi-cui for a refugee lord and his patron.

sentences.zh: 新禮以今無此事，除此一章。

translations.literal: The New Rites deleted this chapter because the circumstance no longer occurs today.
translations.idiomatic: Jin's New Rites dropped the chapter as obsolete.

sentences.zh: 摯虞以為：「《周禮》作于刑厝之時，而著荒政十二。

translations.literal: Zhi Yu argued: "The Zhou Rites were compiled when punishments were laid aside, yet they still list twelve famine policies.
translations.idiomatic: Zhi Yu argued: "The Zhou Rites were compiled when punishments were laid aside, yet they still list twelve famine policies.

sentences.zh: 禮備制待物，不以時衰而除盛典，世隆而闕衰教也。

translations.literal: Rites complete their regulations to meet every contingency—they do not discard great ceremonies because the age declines, nor omit teachings on decline because the world prospers.
translations.idiomatic: Rites complete their regulations to meet every contingency—they do not discard great ceremonies because the age declines, nor omit teachings on decline because the world prospers.

sentences.zh: 曩者王司徒失守播越，自稱寄公。

translations.literal: When former Director Wang lost his command and wandered, calling himself a guest lord.
translations.idiomatic: When former Director Wang lost his command and wandered, calling himself a guest lord.

sentences.zh: 是時天下又多此比，皆禮之所及。

translations.literal: At that time many under Heaven were in the same case—all fell within ritual's reach.
translations.idiomatic: At that time many under Heaven were in the same case—all fell within ritual's reach.

sentences.zh: 宜定新禮自如舊經。」

translations.literal: The New Rites should restore this chapter as in the old classic."
translations.idiomatic: The New Rites should restore this chapter as in the old classic."

sentences.zh: 詔從之。

translations.literal: The edict followed his view."
translations.idiomatic: The throne agreed.

sentences.zh: 漢魏故事無五等諸侯之制，公卿朝士服喪，親疏各如其親。

translations.literal: Han and Wei precedent had no five-rank feudal system; dukes, ministers, and court gentlemen wore mourning close or distant according to true kinship.
translations.idiomatic: Han and Wei let mourning follow blood, not rank.

sentences.zh: 新禮王公五等諸侯成國置卿者，及朝廷公孤之爵，皆傍親絕期，而旁親為之服斬衰，卿校位從大夫者皆絕緦。

translations.literal: The New Rites hold that princes and dukes of the five ranks who have completed a state and installed ministers, together with court duke-and-guardian titles, all cut collateral mourning at qi, yet require collateral kin to wear zhan-cui for them, while ministers ranked with great officers cut si entirely.
translations.idiomatic: Jin's code tried to sever collateral ties for great nobles while still demanding zhan-cui from cousins—a tangle Han never used.

sentences.zh: 摯虞以為：「古者諸侯君臨其國，臣諸父兄，今之諸侯未同于古。

translations.literal: Zhi Yu held: "Ancient feudal lords ruled their states and treated paternal uncles as subjects; today's nobles are not the same as antiquity.
translations.idiomatic: Zhi Yu held: "Ancient feudal lords ruled their states and treated paternal uncles as subjects; today's nobles are not the same as antiquity.

sentences.zh: 未同于古，則其尊未全，不宜便從絕期之制，而令傍親服斬衰之重也。

translations.literal: Because they are not the same as antiquity, their ritual supremacy is incomplete—it is not fitting to follow outright the rule that cuts qi while forcing collateral kin into zhan-cui.
translations.idiomatic: Because they are not the same as antiquity, their ritual supremacy is incomplete—it is not fitting to follow outright the rule that cuts qi while forcing collateral kin into zhan-cui.

sentences.zh: 諸侯既然，則公孤之爵亦宜如舊。

translations.literal: Feudal lords being so, duke-and-guardian titles should likewise follow the old pattern.
translations.idiomatic: Feudal lords being so, duke-and-guardian titles should likewise follow the old pattern.

sentences.zh: 昔魏武帝建安中已曾表上，漢朝依古為制，事與古異，皆不施行，施行者著在魏科。

translations.literal: Wei Emperor Wu in the Jian'an era already memorialized for Han to legislate by antiquity; because affairs differed from antiquity, nothing was enacted, while what was enacted appears in Wei code.
translations.idiomatic: Wei Emperor Wu in the Jian'an era already memorialized for Han to legislate by antiquity; because affairs differed from antiquity, nothing was enacted, while what was enacted appears in Wei code.

sentences.zh: 大晉采以著令，宜定新禮皆如舊。」

translations.literal: Great Jin adopted those entries into promulgated law—the New Rites ought everywhere to match the old statute."
translations.idiomatic: Great Jin adopted those entries into promulgated law—the New Rites ought everywhere to match the old statute."

sentences.zh: 詔從之。

translations.literal: The edict followed this."
translations.idiomatic: The rescript accepted Zhi Yu.

sentences.zh: 《喪服》無弟子為師服之制，新禮弟子為師齊衰三月。

translations.literal: Mourning Garments contains no rule for disciples mourning teachers; the New Rites prescribe qi-cui three months for a teacher.
translations.idiomatic: The revision added three months of qi-cui for masters.

sentences.zh: 摯虞以為：「自古無師服之制，故仲尼之喪，門人疑于所服。

translations.literal: Zhi Yu held: "From antiquity there was no teacher-mourning code—therefore at Confucius's death disciples were unsure what to wear.
translations.idiomatic: Zhi Yu held: "From antiquity there was no teacher-mourning code—therefore at Confucius's death disciples were unsure what to wear.

sentences.zh: 子貢曰：『昔夫子之喪顏回，若喪子而無服，請喪夫子若喪父而無服。』

translations.literal: Zigong said: 'When the Master mourned Yan Hui, it was like mourning a son but without mourning garments; I ask to mourn the Master like mourning a father but without mourning garments.'"
translations.idiomatic: Zigong said: 'When the Master mourned Yan Hui, it was like mourning a son but without mourning garments; I ask to mourn the Master like mourning a father but without mourning garments.'"

sentences.zh: 遂心喪三年。

translations.literal: Thereupon they observed heart mourning three years.
translations.idiomatic: Thereupon they observed heart mourning three years.

sentences.zh: 此則懷三年之哀，而無齊衰之制也。

translations.literal: That harbors three years of grief yet lacks a qi-cui regulation.
translations.idiomatic: That harbors three years of grief yet lacks a qi-cui regulation.

sentences.zh: 群居，入則絰，出則否，所謂弔服加麻也。

translations.literal: When assembled they wore zhui ties indoors but not outdoors—what is called adding hemp to condolence dress.
translations.idiomatic: When assembled they wore zhui ties indoors but not outdoors—what is called adding hemp to condolence dress.

sentences.zh: 先聖為禮，必易從而可傳。

translations.literal: Former sages made ritual easy to follow and possible to transmit.
translations.idiomatic: Former sages made ritual easy to follow and possible to transmit.

sentences.zh: 師徒義誠重，而服制不著，歷代相襲，不以為缺。

translations.literal: Teacher-disciple duty is weighty, yet garment rules were never written down—later ages followed one another and did not treat that as a defect.
translations.idiomatic: Teacher-disciple duty is weighty, yet garment rules were never written down—later ages followed one another and did not treat that as a defect.

sentences.zh: 且尋師者以彌高為得，故屢遷而不嫌；

translations.literal: Moreover those who seek teachers take 'ever higher' as their gain—therefore they change masters repeatedly without scruple;
translations.idiomatic: Moreover those who seek teachers take 'ever higher' as their gain—therefore they change masters repeatedly without scruple;

sentences.zh: 修業者以日新為益，故舍舊而不疑。

translations.literal: those who pursue learning take 'daily renewal' as profit—therefore they cast aside the old without hesitation.
translations.idiomatic: those who pursue learning take 'daily renewal' as profit—therefore they cast aside the old without hesitation.

sentences.zh: 仲尼稱『三人行，必有我師焉』。

translations.literal: Zhongni said, 'In a party of three walking, there must be my teacher among them.'"
translations.idiomatic: Zhongni said, 'In a party of three walking, there must be my teacher among them.'"

sentences.zh: 子貢云，『夫何常師之有』。

translations.literal: Zigong said, 'What constant teacher is there?'"
translations.idiomatic: Zigong said, 'What constant teacher is there?'"

sentences.zh: 淺學之師，暫學之師，不可皆為之服。

translations.literal: Shallow teachers and brief teachers cannot all receive mourning.
translations.idiomatic: Shallow teachers and brief teachers cannot all receive mourning.

sentences.zh: 義有輕重，服有廢興，則臧否由之而起，是非因之而爭，愛惡相攻，悔吝生焉。

translations.literal: When rightness has light and heavy and garments wax and wane, praise and blame arise, yes and no contend, love and hate clash, and regret is born.
translations.idiomatic: When rightness has light and heavy and garments wax and wane, praise and blame arise, yes and no contend, love and hate clash, and regret is born.

sentences.zh: 宜定新禮無服如舊。」

translations.literal: The New Rites should leave teacher mourning absent, as in antiquity."
translations.idiomatic: The New Rites should leave teacher mourning absent, as in antiquity."

sentences.zh: 詔從之。

translations.literal: The edict followed this."
translations.idiomatic: The court agreed.

sentences.zh: 古者天子諸侯葬禮粗備，漢世又多變革，魏晉以下世有改變，大體同漢之制。

translations.literal: In antiquity, the burial rites of Sons of Heaven and feudal lords were roughly complete. In the Han age there were again many changes, and from Wei and Jin downward each generation had alterations, but in broad outline they followed the Han system.
translations.idiomatic: In antiquity, the burial rites of Sons of Heaven and feudal lords were roughly complete. In the Han age there were again many changes, and from Wei and Jin downward each generation had alterations, but in broad outline they followed the Han system.

sentences.zh: 而魏武以禮送終之制，襲稱之數，繁而無益，俗又過之，豫自制送終衣服四篋，題識其上，春秋冬夏，日有不諱，隨時以斂。

translations.literal: Yet Wei Wu held that the rites of sending off the dead and tallies of condolence gifts were excessive without benefit; vulgar practice exceeded them still—so he prepared in advance four chests of burial clothes, labeled for spring, summer, autumn, and winter, to be donned according to whichever season death came.
translations.idiomatic: Cao Cao loathed wasteful obsequies and packed four seasonal shrouds against an unlucky day.

sentences.zh: 金珥珠玉銅鐵之物，一不得送。

translations.literal: Gold, pearls, jade, copper, and iron were forbidden grave goods altogether.
translations.idiomatic: He banned metal and gems from the pit.

sentences.zh: 文帝遵奉，無所增加。

translations.literal: Emperor Wen followed this and added nothing.
translations.idiomatic: Cao Pi kept his father's frugal will.

sentences.zh: 及受禪，刻金璽，追加尊號，不敢開埏，乃為石室，藏璽埏首，以示陵中無金銀諸物也。

translations.literal: When accepting abdication he carved a gold seal and added honor titles yet dared not open the tunnel—so he built a stone chamber at the passage mouth to store the seal, showing the tomb held no gold or silver.
translations.idiomatic: Cao Pi sealed a gold seal in a stone niche to prove the mound stayed bare of treasure.

sentences.zh: 漢禮明器甚多，自是皆省之矣。

translations.literal: Han burials had been rich in mingqi grave goods—from this point onward all were reduced.
translations.idiomatic: Opulent Han figurines gave way to leaner Wei practice.

sentences.zh: 魏文帝黃初三年，又自作終制曰：「禮，國君即位為椑，存不忘亡也。

translations.literal: In the third year of Huangchu under Emperor Wen of Wei, he also personally composed final regulations, saying, "According to ritual, when a ruler of a state takes the throne, he prepares an outer coffin; while alive, he does not forget death.
translations.idiomatic: In the third year of Huangchu under Emperor Wen of Wei, he also personally composed final regulations, saying, "According to ritual, when a ruler of a state takes the throne, he prepares an outer coffin; while alive, he does not forget death.

sentences.zh: 壽陵因山為體，無封樹，無立寢殿，造園邑，通神道。

translations.literal: His Shou mausoleum follows the mountain's contour—no mound, no trees, no resting hall, no park district, no spirit road opened.
translations.idiomatic: His Shou mausoleum follows the mountain's contour—no mound, no trees, no resting hall, no park district, no spirit road opened.

sentences.zh: 夫葬者藏也，欲人之不得見也。

translations.literal: Burial means hiding—wishing men not to see.
translations.idiomatic: Burial means hiding—wishing men not to see.

sentences.zh: 禮不墓祭，欲存亡不黷也。

translations.literal: Ritual forbids sacrifice at the grave—wishing the living and dead not to profane one another.
translations.idiomatic: Ritual forbids sacrifice at the grave—wishing the living and dead not to profane one another.

sentences.zh: 皇后及貴人以下不隨王之國者，有終沒，皆葬澗西，前又已表其處矣。」

translations.literal: Empresses and honored ladies who do not follow the prince to his fief and who die in the end are all buried west of the Jian River; I have already marked the ground."
translations.idiomatic: Empresses and honored ladies who do not follow the prince to his fief and who die in the end are all buried west of the Jian River; I have already marked the ground."

sentences.zh: 此詔藏之宗廟，副在尚書、秘書、三府。

translations.literal: This edict was deposited in the ancestral temple; copies went to the Masters of Writing, Palace Library, and the Three Offices."
translations.idiomatic: Copies of the will rested in the temple and chief ministries.

sentences.zh: 明帝亦遵奉之。

translations.literal: Ming-di likewise followed it.
translations.idiomatic: Cao Rui obeyed the same will.

sentences.zh: 明帝性雖崇奢，然未遽營陵墓之制也。

translations.literal: Though Ming-di's nature inclined to luxury, he still did not rush to build an extravagant mausoleum system.
translations.idiomatic: Even the lavish Cao Rui held back on tomb scale.

sentences.zh: 宣帝豫自于首陽山為土藏，不填不樹，作《顧命終制》，斂以時服，不設明器。

translations.literal: Emperor Xuan in advance prepared an earthen burial chamber on Mount Shouyang—no mound, no trees—and composed the 'Charge at Gu' end testament: shroud in seasonal clothes only, with no ming vessels.
translations.idiomatic: Sima Yi dug a plain shaft on Shouyang, left the hill unmarked, and left written orders for everyday clothes and no grave goods.

sentences.zh: 景、文皆謹奉成命，無所加焉。

translations.literal: Emperor Jing and Emperor Wen both scrupulously obeyed the completed testament and added nothing to it.
translations.idiomatic: Sima Shi and Sima Zhao kept Cao Pi's austere burial instructions to the letter.

sentences.zh: 景帝崩，喪事制度又依宣帝故事。

translations.literal: When Emperor Jing died, the funeral regulations again followed Emperor Xuan's precedent.
translations.idiomatic: Sima Shi's obsequies copied Sima Yi's lean model.

sentences.zh: 武帝泰始四年，文明王皇后崩，將合葬，開崇陽陵，使太尉司馬望奉祭，進皇帝密璽綬于便房神坐。

translations.literal: In the fourth year of Taishi under Emperor Wu, when Empress Wenming Wang died and was about to be jointly buried, Chongyang Mausoleum was opened, Grand Commandant Sima Wang was sent to present sacrifice, and the emperor's sealed jade seal and cords were advanced to the spirit seat in the side chamber.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth year of Taishi under Emperor Wu, when Empress Wenming Wang died and was about to be jointly buried, Chongyang Mausoleum was opened, Grand Commandant Sima Wang was sent to present sacrifice, and the emperor's sealed jade seal and cords were advanced to the spirit seat in the side chamber.

sentences.zh: 魏氏金璽，此又儉矣。

translations.literal: Wei's gold seal—another mark of frugality.
translations.idiomatic: Even the golden seal bespoke restraint.

sentences.zh: 江左初，元、明崇儉，且百度草創，山陵奉終，省約備矣。

translations.literal: Early in the southward court, Emperors Yuan and Ming prized simplicity; the hundred offices were still being founded, so imperial tombs stayed spare yet adequate.
translations.idiomatic: When the court fled across the Yangzi, Sima Rui and Sima Shao kept burials modest while institutions were new.

sentences.zh: 成帝咸康七年，皇后杜氏崩。

translations.literal: In the seventh Xiankang year of Emperor Cheng, Empress Du died.
translations.idiomatic: Empress Du of Cheng passed in 341.

sentences.zh: 詔外官五日一入臨，內官旦一入而已，過葬虞祭禮畢止。

translations.literal: An edict ordered outer officials to enter condolence only once every five days and inner staff once at dawn, ending once burial and the Yu rite were finished.
translations.idiomatic: Courtiers could wail only on that thin schedule until the post-burial service closed mourning.

sentences.zh: 有司奏，大行皇后陵所作凶門柏歷門，號顯陽端門。

translations.literal: The offices proposed building a funeral gate and cypress "calendar" portal for the late empress's mound, to be named the Xianyang gate.
translations.idiomatic: The ministry wanted a formal death-gate and cypress lintel named like a palace portal.

sentences.zh: 詔曰：「門如所處。

translations.literal: The edict read: "Let the gate stand where proposed.
translations.idiomatic: The edict read: "Let the gate stand where proposed.

sentences.zh: 凶門柏歷，大為煩費，停之。」

translations.literal: Funeral gates and cypress calendars are extravagantly costly—suspend them."
translations.idiomatic: Funeral gates and cypress calendars are extravagantly costly—suspend them."

sentences.zh: 案蔡謨說，以二瓦器盛始死之祭，繫於木，裹以葦席，置庭中，近南，名為重，今之凶門是其象也。

translations.literal: Cai Mo explains that two earthen jars holding the first-death offerings were lashed to a frame, wrapped in reed matting, and set in the courtyard toward the south as a chong; today's funeral gate imitates that form.
translations.idiomatic: Cai Mo traced the "death gate" to the temporary chong bundle hung south of the yard.

sentences.zh: 禮，既虞而作主，今未葬，未有主，故以重當之。

translations.literal: By ritual one fashions the spirit tablet after the Yu rite; before burial there is no tablet, so the chong stands in for it.
translations.idiomatic: Until the tablet existed, the chong served as the spirit's lodging.

sentences.zh: 禮稱為主道，此其義也。

translations.literal: The canon calls this the "lord-of-the-spirit path"—that is the idea.
translations.idiomatic: Classical glosses treat the chong as the spirit's interim path.

sentences.zh: 范堅又曰：「凶門非禮，禮有懸重，形似凶門。

translations.literal: Fan Jian adds: "The funeral gate is not canonical; ritual only suspends a chong that merely resembles a gate.
translations.idiomatic: Fan Jian adds: "The funeral gate is not canonical; ritual only suspends a chong that merely resembles a gate.

sentences.zh: 後人出之門外以表喪，俗遂行之。

translations.literal: Later generations moved it outside the gate to advertise mourning, and vulgar custom adopted it.
translations.idiomatic: Later generations moved it outside the gate to advertise mourning, and vulgar custom adopted it.

sentences.zh: 薄帳，即古弔幕之類也。」

translations.literal: Thin curtains belong to the ancient class of mourning screens."
translations.idiomatic: Thin curtains belong to the ancient class of mourning screens."

sentences.zh: 是時，又詔曰：「重壤之下，豈宜崇飾無用，陵中唯潔掃而已。」

translations.literal: Another edict then declared: "Beneath double layers of earth one should not lavish useless ornament; only sweep the vault clean."
translations.idiomatic: Another edict then declared: "Beneath double layers of earth one should not lavish useless ornament; only sweep the vault clean."

sentences.zh: 有司又奏，依舊選公卿以下六品子弟六十人為挽郎，詔又停之。

translations.literal: The offices again asked to conscript sixty youths of sixth rank and below as catafalque pullers, as of old; the edict again refused.
translations.idiomatic: Officials wanted sixty noble sons as rope-pullers; the throne again said no.

sentences.zh: 孝武帝太元四年九月，皇后王氏崩。

translations.literal: In the ninth month of the fourth year of Taiyuan under Emperor Xiaowu, Empress Wang died.
translations.idiomatic: In the ninth month of the fourth year of Taiyuan under Emperor Xiaowu, Empress Wang died.

sentences.zh: 詔曰：「終事唯從儉速。」

translations.literal: An edict said: "Finish everything frugally and quickly."
translations.idiomatic: An edict said: "Finish everything frugally and quickly."

sentences.zh: 又詔：「遠近不得遣山陵使。」

translations.literal: Another edict said, “Neither near nor distant officials may send envoys to the imperial tombs.”
translations.idiomatic: Another edict said, “Neither near nor distant officials may send envoys to the imperial tombs.”

sentences.zh: 有司奏選挽郎二十四人，詔停之。

translations.literal: When the ministry asked for twenty-four pullers, the edict stopped that as well.
translations.idiomatic: Even twenty-four rope-boys were denied.

sentences.zh: 古無墓祭之禮。

translations.literal: Antiquity knew no sacrifices at the tomb itself.
translations.idiomatic: The classics never sanctioned grave-side worship.

sentences.zh: 漢承秦，皆有園寢。

translations.literal: Han continued Qin and maintained park-like resting shrines at every imperial mound.
translations.idiomatic: Han kept Qin's tomb parks and resting halls.

sentences.zh: 正月上丁，祠南郊禮畢，次北郊、明堂、高廟、世祖廟，謂之五供。

translations.literal: On the upper ding day of the first month, after the southern suburban sacrifice, the court in sequence offered at the northern suburb, the Bright Hall, the High Temple, and Emperor Shizu's shrine—the so-called five offerings.
translations.idiomatic: The capital's spring round moved from the southern altar through the northern rites in fixed order.

sentences.zh: 魏武葬高陵，有司依漢立陵上祭殿。

translations.literal: Cao Cao was buried at Gaoling; the ministry, following Han, built a sacrificial hall atop the tumulus.
translations.idiomatic: Wei still raised a tomb-shrine over Gaoling, aping Han.

sentences.zh: 至文帝黃初三年，乃詔曰：「先帝躬履節儉，遺詔省約。

translations.literal: In the third year of Huangchu under Emperor Wen, he then issued an edict, saying, "The late emperor personally practiced frugality, and his final edict was sparing and restrained.
translations.idiomatic: In the third year of Huangchu under Emperor Wen, he then issued an edict, saying, "The late emperor personally practiced frugality, and his final edict was sparing and restrained.

sentences.zh: 子以述父為孝，臣以繫事為忠。

translations.literal: The son expresses filial piety by carrying out the father's words; the minister shows loyalty by continuing his tasks.
translations.idiomatic: The son expresses filial piety by carrying out the father's words; the minister shows loyalty by continuing his tasks.

sentences.zh: 古不墓祭，皆設於廟。

translations.literal: The ancients never sacrificed at graves—everything was set in the ancestral temple.
translations.idiomatic: The ancients never sacrificed at graves—everything was set in the ancestral temple.

sentences.zh: 高陵上殿皆毀壞，車馬還廄，衣服藏府，以從先帝儉德之志。」

translations.literal: Destroy the upper halls at Gaoling; return carriages and horses to the stables and store garments in the treasury, to match the late emperor's wish for thrift."
translations.idiomatic: Destroy the upper halls at Gaoling; return carriages and horses to the stables and store garments in the treasury, to match the late emperor's wish for thrift."

sentences.zh: 文帝自作終制，又曰「壽陵無立寢殿，造園邑」，自後園邑寢殿遂絕。

translations.literal: Emperor Wen personally made his final regulations and further said, “At Shouling do not establish a resting hall or build a tomb settlement”; from then on tomb settlements and resting halls ceased.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Wen personally made his final regulations and further said, “At Shouling do not establish a resting hall or build a tomb settlement”; from then on tomb settlements and resting halls ceased.

sentences.zh: 齊王在位九年，始一謁高平陵而曹爽誅，其後遂廢，終於魏世。

translations.literal: The prince of Qi reigned nine years before he once visited Gaoling; after Cao Shuang's execution the practice was abandoned for the rest of Wei.
translations.idiomatic: Cao Fang's single visit to Gaoling ended with Cao Shuang's purge, and Wei rulers stopped touring tombs.

sentences.zh: 及宣帝，遺詔「子弟群官皆不得謁陵」。

translations.literal: Emperor Xuan's testament commanded that "sons, younger kin, and all officials must not visit the imperial tombs."
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Xuan's testament commanded that "sons, younger kin, and all officials must not visit the imperial tombs."

sentences.zh: 於是景、文遵旨。

translations.literal: Jing and Wen obeyed that order.
translations.idiomatic: Sima Shi and Sima Zhao complied.

sentences.zh: 至武帝，猶再謁崇陽陵，一謁峻平陵，然遂不敢謁高原陵，至惠帝復止也。

translations.literal: Emperor Wu still visited Chongyang twice and Junping once, yet never dared approach Gaoling; under Emperor Hui the custom lapsed again.
translations.idiomatic: Sima Yan alone made limited visits, never to Cao Cao's mound, and Hui abandoned the habit entirely.

sentences.zh: 逮于江左，元帝崩後，諸公始有謁陵辭告之事。

translations.literal: After the move south of the Yangzi, not until Emperor Yuan died did high nobles begin visiting mausoleums to announce their leave-takings.
translations.idiomatic: Eastern Jin nobles only began tomb pilgrimages after Sima Rui's death.

sentences.zh: 蓋由眷同友執，率情而舉，非洛京之舊也。

translations.literal: They acted from private friendship among peers, not from Luoyang precedent.
translations.idiomatic: The practice sprang from camaraderie's impulse, not old capital law.

sentences.zh: 成帝時，中宮亦年年拜陵，議者以為非禮，於是遂止，以為永制。

translations.literal: Under Emperor Cheng the inner palace yearly visited tombs until critics called it uncanonical; the court then banned it permanently.
translations.idiomatic: Cheng's harem stopped annual tomb trips once ritualists objected.

sentences.zh: 至穆帝時，褚太后臨朝，又拜陵，帝幼故也。

translations.literal: Under Emperor Mu, Empress Dowager Chu regent, tombs were visited again because the boy emperor was young.
translations.idiomatic: Mu's regent mother revived the visits while the sovereign was a child.

sentences.zh: 至孝武崩，驃騎將軍司馬道子曰：「今雖權制釋服，至於朔望諸節，自應展情陵所，以一周為斷。」

translations.literal: After Xiaowu died, Sima Daozi said: "Though we have shortened mourning by expedient rule, on new and full moons and festivals we should still show feeling at the tomb—take one round as the limit."
translations.idiomatic: After Xiaowu died, Sima Daozi said: "Though we have shortened mourning by expedient rule, on new and full moons and festivals we should still show feeling at the tomb—take one round as the limit."

sentences.zh: 於是至陵，變服單衣，煩黷無準，非禮意也。

translations.literal: Thereupon courtiers went to the tombs in thin single garments—endless fuss with no standard, contrary to ritual intent.
translations.idiomatic: The result was slovenly dress and chaotic etiquette at every visit.

sentences.zh: 及安帝元興元年，尚書左僕射桓謙奏：「百僚拜陵，起于中興，非晉舊典，積習生常，遂為近法。

translations.literal: In the first year of Yuanxing under Emperor An, Huan Qian, Left Vice Director of the Secretariat, memorialized, "The hundred officials paying respects at the mausoleum began with the Restoration and was not an old Jin statute. Accumulated practice produced a norm, and it consequently became a recent rule.
translations.idiomatic: In the first year of Yuanxing under Emperor An, Huan Qian, Left Vice Director of the Secretariat, memorialized, "The hundred officials paying respects at the mausoleum began with the Restoration and was not an old Jin statute. Accumulated practice produced a norm, and it consequently became a recent rule.

sentences.zh: 尋武皇帝詔，乃不使人主諸王拜陵，豈唯百僚！

translations.literal: Review Emperor Wu's edict: he forbade even the sovereign and princes from tomb visits—let alone mere officials!
translations.idiomatic: Review Emperor Wu's edict: he forbade even the sovereign and princes from tomb visits—let alone mere officials!

sentences.zh: 謂宜遵奉。」

translations.literal: We ought to obey that precedent."
translations.idiomatic: We ought to obey that precedent."

sentences.zh: 於是施行。

translations.literal: The measure was implemented.
translations.idiomatic: The ban took effect.

sentences.zh: 及義熙初，又復江左之舊，

translations.literal: Early in the Yixi era the southern custom briefly returned.
translations.idiomatic: Yixi reopened tomb pilgrimages for a time.
